title: Choose Scholar's visual world
question: Select the direction that should carry the full research workspace across every page.

options.label: The Finding Aid
options.lineage: Special-collections finding aids, archival index cards, ruled dockets
options.thesis: A living finding aid for research evidence, not a generic admin dashboard.
options.viewport: A three-column research desk: folio index, cited conversation, evidence register.
options.risk: Archive references become clutter if task hierarchy is not strict.

raised.raise: Critical, pending, and stale states also change line weight and dash.
A live key rail connects navigation, citation markers, and evidence entries.
Catalog numerals and specimen rhythm give dense metadata an editorial scale.

options.label: The Review Dossier
options.lineage: Peer-review dossiers, redlined manuscripts, editorial registration marks
options.thesis: The workspace as a live peer-review dossier with claims and evidence in the margin.
options.viewport: A manuscript-centered workspace with evidence hanging in a red-ruled margin.
options.risk: Literal paper cues can make the product feel slower than the task.

options.label: The Ruled Reference
options.lineage: Scholarly reference setting and ruled annotation margins
options.thesis: A precise reference edition where a center rail anchors navigation and citations.
options.viewport: A wide-margin reading desk with a narrow live key rail between work areas.
options.case: Very strong academic identification; risks making every control feel annotation-like.
options.risk: A universal key rail can slow scanning when users need quick task switching.

options.label: The Emission Rail
options.lineage: Spectroscopic plates and scientific wavelength notation
options.thesis: Service, retrieval, and evidence states register on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: A dark research bench where one rail connects model, retrieval, and evidence state.
options.case: Strong technical signal; risks reading as an instrument rather than a workspace.
options.risk: Spectral colors and slim traces can hurt state recognition at a glance.

options.label: The Specimen Sheet
options.lineage: Emigre bitmap type specimens and editorial specimen books
options.thesis: The workspace as a bold scholarly specimen sheet with machine-readable labels.
options.viewport: A high-contrast specimen grid led by oversized catalog numerals.
options.case: Memorable identity; lower immediate clarity for a dense operational tool.
options.risk: Display typography can overpower the evidence users came to inspect.

options.label: The Character Roster
options.thesis: Documents and evidence arranged as a playful ranked roster.
options.viewport: A bright roster of papers with oversized personality plates.
options.risk: Would make serious evidence look like merchandise.
options.kept: Whole-cell selection states remain useful for the document index.

options.label: The Research Map
options.lineage: Illustrated zoo and gardens guide maps
options.thesis: Research spaces as adjacent colored territories around a central graph.
options.viewport: A full-frame living map around the citation network.
options.case: Excellent spatial identity, poor fit for dense document tasks.
options.risk: The metaphor would dominate every utilitarian action.
options.kept: One geometry driving graph, layout, and selection remains a useful discipline.

options.label: The Folded Dossier
options.lineage: Handwritten cassette J-cards and folded inlays
options.thesis: Research sessions as folded dossiers with side A and side B views.
options.viewport: A research session folded between question and evidence views.
options.case: Memorable folding behavior, weak academic authority.
options.risk: The formal play would obscure standard navigation.
options.kept: Spine and fold hierarchy can improve mobile route switching.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean three-column research tool executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Familiar sidebar, document list, chat, and evidence panels.
